quote: Busy shared 24-hour kitchen cooking curry, buffalo wings, kebabs, sandwiches and pancakes together; high ambient wheat/flour use
found: Official menu: 24時間営業 年中無休 / カレーうどん 1,000円 / サバサンド / ファラフェルサンド / サクラパンケーキ / シナモンアップルパイ / フィッシュ＆チップス — one 24h kitchen, heavy wheat load.
method: plain fetch of official menu + Gnavi item list
note: Substance holds and is now citable, but two named items are wrong: 'buffalo wings' appears on no Sakura Cafe menu past or present, and the halal kebab bowl was 2020-era (Visit Chiyoda) and is gone from the 2026 menu — replace them with the real wheat carriers (カレーうどん udon, サバサンド/ファラフェルサンド, パンケーキ, フィッシュ＆チップス, アップルパイ).

quote: GF pancakes appear to be a marketed option but no dedicated GF griddle/fryer/prep area was found in any source
found: "Other than that, the gluten-free pancakes, vegetarian dishes, and even halal dishes for Muslims are very popular among guests, too." (Visit Chiyoda, 2020-03-13)
method: Yahoo Japan search for the venue + Chiyoda tourism article
note: The GF-pancake claim is real but STALE: its only evidence is a 2020 Chiyoda tourism piece quoting staff. The current official menu lists only サクラパンケーキ 750円 and NY風チョコレートパンケーキ with no gluten-free designation anywhere, so the 'marketed option' framing should be dated or dropped. No dedicated GF surface is claimed by anyone — that half stands.

quote: Curries and sauces likely use wheat-based Japanese soy sauce; unverified
found: サクラカレー　（日本）800円 —「よもだそば」特製のそばつゆを配合した和風インドカレー。
method: plain fetch of the Gnavi food menu
note: This is no longer 'unverified' — the house curry is explicitly built on Yomoda Soba's soba tsuyu, which is koikuchi-shoyu based and therefore wheat. Upgrade the wording from 'likely/unverified' to a documented wheat pathway and cite the Gnavi menu.

quote: Standard curries/sauces presumed to use wheat-containing koikuchi soy sauce; confirm before ordering
found: サクラカレー　（日本）—「よもだそば」特製のそばつゆを配合した和風インドカレー。
method: plain fetch of the Gnavi food menu
note: Same evidence: drop 'presumed', the shop's own menu names a soba-tsuyu base for the signature curry. Keep the 'confirm before ordering' advice.

quote: Meat and dairy cooked in the same kitchen; signature Sakura Curry contains chicken
found: サクラカレー is described only as 「よもだそば」特製のそばつゆを配合した和風インドカレー — no chicken. The chicken dish on this menu is マフェ 900円「ピーナッツペーストを使ったトマトと鶏肉のシチュー。セネガルの家庭料理です！」
method: plain fetch of the Gnavi food menu + official menu
note: First half is solidly supported (牛肉のトマト煮込みロモサルタード, マタルパニール cottage cheese, カリーブルスト pork sausage, プティン, フィッシュ＆チップス all in one kitchen). The second half is WRONG: no source puts chicken in Sakura Curry — that belongs to the Senegalese マフェ. A detail transplanted from a different dish; correct or delete it.

quote: Confirm falafel/vegetable items are not fried in shared meat oil
found: SNACK section: フライドポテト 650円 / フィッシュ＆チップス 700円 / カリーブルスト 680円 — a fried fish item and fries share the snack line; ファラフェルサンド 1,000円 is on the same kitchen's menu.
method: plain fetch of the Gnavi food menu
note: The advice is sound and now citable. Sharpen it: the shared-oil hazard here is wheat-battered フィッシュ＆チップス, which is a gluten risk as well as a vegan one — worth mirroring into gf_cross_contamination.

quote: English-speaking, multilingual staff experienced with international guests
found: Gnavi shop info: 外国語対応 メニュー「英語」/ スタッフ「英語 中国語 スペイン語」; Visit Chiyoda: "Guests in this cafe come from over 100 countries around the world."
method: plain fetch of Gnavi JSON payload + Chiyoda article

quote: Per-item allergen pictograms shown on some menu items (e.g. chicken, dairy, root vegetables flagged)
method: official site menu, Gnavi full food+drink menu, Visit Chiyoda article, Wayback 2023 menu — none carries allergen icons
note: No Sakura Cafe menu surface shows per-item allergen pictograms. The specific trio 'chicken, dairy, root vegetables' is a T's Restaurant style marker (root-vegetable/allium flagging is the oriental-vegetarian convention used by T's たんたん, two records away in this same shard) — this reads as a detail transplanted from another venue. Delete it; it would tell a celiac the menu carries allergen labelling that does not exist.

quote: Openly markets gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan and halal options
found: Visit Chiyoda (2020): "the gluten-free pancakes, vegetarian dishes, and even halal dishes for Muslims are very popular" — vegetarian, GF and halal only, and only in 2020.
method: Chiyoda article + current official menu + Gnavi menu + Wayback
note: 'Vegan' is supported by nothing, anywhere — the shop's word is ベジタリアン (ベジタリアンカレー, ファラフェルサンド「ベジタリアンメニュー」), never ヴィーガン. GF and halal have only 2020 evidence and neither appears on the 2026 menu. As written this positive over-sells the venue to both audiences; restate as 'vegetarian dishes labelled on the menu; GF pancakes and halal reported in 2020, unconfirmed since'.

method: plain fetch of Gnavi shop info

note: Duplicate of the staff_allergy_handling pictogram claim and equally unfounded. Remove both.

quote: Organic vegetables sourced from a Tohoku farm
found: Gnavi こだわり「東北牧場直送の自然栽培野菜&野草」…「サクラカフェでは青森にある東北牧場の無農薬環境で自生した野草を料理やドリンクとしてご提供しております」; menu:「東北牧場の残留農薬ゼロの青い卵を使用した贅沢なプリン」
method: plain fetch of Gnavi こだわり block; corroborated by Visit Chiyoda 「カフェ直営の青森にある東北牧場で採れた完全無農薬のお野菜のサラダ」
note: True and now citable. Precision: 東北牧場 is the group's own farm in AOMORI (Tohoku region), and the sourcing is 無農薬/自然栽培 wild herbs, vegetables and eggs — not a certified 'organic' scheme. Carries no gluten implication.

9 of 12 claims are true but carried no citation at all; all now have a live URL. Three are defective: chicken wrongly attributed to Sakura Curry, allergen pictograms that exist on no menu (claimed twice), and a 'vegan' marketing claim with zero support. gf 'ask' is correct — a 24h shared kitchen running curry udon, fish & chips and a soba-tsuyu curry base cannot go higher.

why: Every plant-forward item this venue publishes is labelled ベジタリアン, never ヴィーガン: ベジタリアンカレー and ファラフェルサンド carry no dairy/egg disclosure, and the dessert/drink line is dairy- and honey-heavy (マタルパニール cottage cheese, 青玉プリン made of egg+milk+honey, プティン). No source in Japanese or English uses the word vegan for this branch, so 'options' asserts a confirmed vegan path that no publisher has confirmed.
